about: The `idlocation` of a <send> names a string variable the machine writes the id it generates for the send to, and a later <cancel sendidexpr> names that variable: `arm` sends two delayed events under ids of their own, and `cancel.first` removes only the one whose id `first` holds. An id belongs to one execution of the send: `arm` run twice leaves four sends waiting under four ids, and `cancel.first` removes the latest of the two it made. The id is written before the send reads any other argument, so `armfail`, whose `delayexpr` cannot be evaluated, still leaves `first` holding the id of the send it discarded: the <cancel> that follows removes nothing, and the earlier send comes due. Every send waits 200 ms and every check stands at least 50 ms from a deadline. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: two sends are armed, each under an id of its own
`first` holds the id of the first send: only that send is removed
the wait is over: only the second send comes due
armed a second time: four sends wait under four ids, and the variables hold the latest two
`first` holds the id of the latest first send: only that one is removed
three sends come due: the earlier first send, and both second sends
armed again, and `first` holds the id of its first send
the delay cannot be computed: the message is discarded and error.execution is raised, but the id was written first
`first` holds the id of the send that was discarded: no send holds it, so nothing is removed
both sends of the last `arm` come due
